evaluated.name: EVYieldCleanWorkingCapital
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Enterprise-level cheapness (EBITDA/EV) is trustworthy only when operating profitability is not being manufactured by working-capital build-ups in receivables and inventory.
evaluated.reasoning: EBITDA/EV neutralizes leverage and cash holdings so cheapness is measured on operating assets, while the change in non-cash working capital captures the specific accrual channel (receivables/inventory inflation) that contaminates EBITDA. Combining them should separate genuinely cheap operating businesses from those whose EBITDA is a working-capital illusion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ValueCleanSloanAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Book-to-market earns a premium only when reported profits are not produced by working-capital build-up net of depreciation; accrual-heavy cheap firms are value traps.
evaluated.reasoning: The accrual leg is the balance-sheet Sloan measure (change in working capital minus depreciation) scaled by assets, built from theme-exclusive items `wcap` and `dp` that are reported far more broadly than cash-flow-statement components, which should lift coverage well above the 0.11 of the accepted gen-0 signal. Ranking both legs makes the long book cheap-and-clean and the short book expensive-and-accrual-laden, the exact intersection the economic story requires.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SloanCashEarningsYield
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: The correct value multiple is price relative to accrual-purged cash earnings; firms cheap on cash earnings outperform, and firms that look cheap only on GAAP income do not.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of blending two ranks, this embeds the accrual correction inside the valuation ratio itself, so accruals change the measured cheapness rather than acting as a separate filter — a distinguishable structural test against Signal 1. Using `dp` and `DELTA(wcap,1)` keeps coverage high while making the numerator an approximation of cash flow available to equity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualLoadPerMarketValue
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: Scaling accruals by market equity rather than assets measures how large the non-cash component of earnings is relative to what investors paid; this is the defining quantitative feature of a value trap.
evaluated.reasoning: The price deflator makes the variable jointly large for cheap firms and for accrual-inflated firms, so the short leg concentrates precisely on low-priced companies whose earnings are least cash-backed and most likely to reverse. It also serves as a clean diagnostic of whether the interaction's return predictability lives in the trap (short) side rather than the quality-value (long) side.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapAndCleanConjunction
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Value and accounting quality are complements, not substitutes: a firm must be both cheap and cash-backed to earn the premium, so the weaker of the two ranks should govern expected returns.
evaluated.reasoning: SUMRANK lets an extreme value rank compensate for terrible accruals (and vice versa), whereas MIN enforces the conjunction and should sharpen the long leg toward genuine quality-value names. Comparing this against Signal 1 isolates the aggregation choice while holding the underlying economic channels fixed, telling us whether the FF5 alpha comes from the intersection or from linear averaging.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CumulativeBloatValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What contaminates cheapness is not a single year's accrual but a multi-year accumulation of unconfirmed accruals (balance-sheet bloat), which must eventually be reversed or written off.
evaluated.reasoning: A five-year cumulative accrual sum captures the stock of soft assets embedded in book equity, which is exactly why a high book-to-market can be illusory — the book value itself is inflated. This changes the economic channel from annual earnings quality to the reliability of the denominator-free book anchor, a mechanism a one-year accrual cannot express.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SalesYieldRevenueQuality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Sales-to-price cheapness is trustworthy only if revenue is converting to cash; rising non-cash current assets per dollar of sales signals channel-stuffing or inventory accumulation that will reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: This swaps the valuation anchor to a revenue multiple (immune to earnings management in the numerator) and pairs it with an operating-quality ratio measuring how many non-cash current assets are needed to generate a dollar of sales, a distinct accrual channel from net income minus cash flow. If sales-based value works better than book- or earnings-based value once revenue quality is imposed, the interaction is about revenue recognition rather than earnings smoothing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashVsAccrualYieldWedge
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Investors anchor on the earnings multiple; firms that are cheap on accrual-purged cash earnings but not cheap on reported earnings are systematically underpriced, and the reverse for accrual-inflated earnings multiples.
evaluated.reasoning: Both legs are price-deflated yield ranks, so their difference is nearly HML-neutral by construction and isolates the wedge created purely by accruals — precisely the orthogonality the archive's negative FF5 alphas say we need. If this delivers positive alpha where the SUMRANK composites failed, the mispricing lives in the accrual wedge and not in cheapness itself.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ValueScaledAccrualLoad
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The accrual anomaly is concentrated in cheap, neglected firms where information quality is low and arbitrage costly; expensive growth firms' accruals are already scrutinized.
evaluated.reasoning: Here accruals set the sign and cheapness only scales the magnitude, so the long-short book is clean-cheap versus dirty-cheap — both legs are value names, cancelling much of the HML/CMA loading that destroyed the earlier composites. Winsorizing before z-scoring prevents microcap accrual outliers from driving portfolio composition, a likely contributor to the unstable spreads seen so far.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IndNeutralCleanValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cross-industry differences in normal book-to-market and normal accrual intensity (capital-intensive versus working-capital-intensive sectors) contaminate the raw composite; within-industry cheapness backed by within-industry clean accounting is the real mispricing.
evaluated.reasoning: This holds the economic channels of ValueCleanSloanAccruals fixed and changes only the neutralization, so it cleanly diagnoses whether the negative FF5 alpha came from industry-level value/investment tilts absorbed by HML and CMA. If alpha turns positive, industry neutralization is the design lever worth consolidating in later generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConservativeDepreciationValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(dp, at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is more credible when accounting is conservative: firms charging heavy depreciation understate current earnings and book value, so their low price reflects accounting conservatism rather than genuine economic decline.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the working-capital accrual channel with the long-lived-asset accrual channel — depreciation adequacy — which is a distinct source of earnings quality and is not what the Sloan measure captures. It also uses only current-year levels, so it should show whether the archive's stuck 0.11 coverage is driven by the two-year requirement of DELTA(wcap, 1).
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardBookToMarket
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), lct)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: A high book-to-market is only informative if book equity is composed of hard assets (cash and fixed capital) rather than soft accrual assets; stripping non-cash working capital out of book equity should isolate defensible value.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than filtering value with a separate quality score, this repairs the value measure's numerator, so the resulting spread is a *different* value factor rather than HML plus a quality tilt — a structurally distinct route to non-spanned alpha. Soft-asset-heavy book equity is exactly what gets written down in value traps, so removing it should shift the long leg away from the traps.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RevenueCashQualityValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Sales-based cheapness is trustworthy only when revenue is collected in cash; direct cash-flow-statement changes in receivables and inventory measure collection quality far more precisely than balance-sheet differences.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash-flow-statement items recch and invch are signed as cash inflows, so higher values mean receivables and inventory are shrinking, i.e. revenue converting to cash, giving a cleaner quality channel than the noisy balance-sheet delta used earlier. Pairing it with a revenue multiple keeps the valuation anchor immune to earnings management, and comparing its coverage and alpha against Signal 1 tells us whether measurement precision or factor-neutrality is the binding constraint.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapFirmPercentAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), ABS(ib)), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among cheap firms, the fraction of reported profit that is accrual rather than cash determines whether cheapness is opportunity or trap; percent accruals (accruals per dollar of earnings) measures that reliance directly, unlike asset-scaled accruals.
evaluated.reasoning: The indicator restricts the signal to above-average book-to-market firms and sets everything else to zero, so the sorted long-short book is clean-cheap versus dirty-cheap — a value-neutral accrual spread whose HML and CMA loadings largely cancel, addressing the mechanical source of the archive's negative alphas. Percent accruals is also a stronger measure of earnings reliance than accruals/assets because it scales by the earnings actually being questioned.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapFirmCashStatementAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0), NEG(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Within the cheap universe, the specific accruals that reverse are receivable, inventory and payable movements; measuring them from the cash-flow statement rather than balance-sheet differences removes acquisition and restatement noise.
evaluated.reasoning: This holds the value-neutral gating structure of Signal 1 fixed and changes only the accrual measurement, so together the pair isolates whether the weak within-value accrual spread reflects a genuine absence of mispricing or noisy balance-sheet accrual proxies. Coverage will be lower (cash-flow items start later), which is exactly the precision-versus-breadth trade we need quantified.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ValueAccrualImprovement
evaluated.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A cheap firm becomes investable when its earnings stop being accrual-driven; the transition from accrual-inflated to cash-backed earnings is the moment the value trap resolves, and investors underreact to it.
evaluated.reasoning: The level of accruals may already be reflected in price after years of persistence, whereas the first difference is news about accounting quality and is a change variable with little factor loading. Gating on cheapness keeps the spread value-neutral, so any alpha here is genuinely non-spanned by FF5 rather than a repackaged HML tilt.

evaluated.name: EVYieldLowWorkingCapitalStock
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Enterprise-value cheapness backed by a lean working-capital balance sheet identifies firms whose operating profits are cash-converting; a large stock of working capital is accumulated soft assets awaiting reversal.
evaluated.reasoning: The EV-anchored gen-0 signal was the only construction with non-negative alpha and a decent Sharpe, suggesting enterprise-level cheapness is less collinear with HML than book-to-market, but its one-year working-capital delta was noisy and cost coverage. Replacing the delta with the working-capital *stock* keeps the same economic channel (balance-sheet bloat), drops the two-year data requirement, and should raise coverage toward the 0.137 seen for level-based measures.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PayoutNotCoveredByCashEarnings
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(dvc, SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: The classic value trap is a high-yield, cheap firm distributing cash it is not generating; a dividend exceeding accrual-purged cash earnings is an unsustainable payout that precedes cuts and price declines.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a distinct mechanism — payout sustainability rather than earnings quality per se — and it is high precisely for the optically attractive names (high dividend yield, low price) that pure value screens buy, so its short leg should sit inside the value universe rather than in glamour stocks. Because both the trap and non-trap firms are cheap dividend payers, the spread should be far less HML-loaded than the earlier composites.

evaluated.name: NetCashValueCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The most defensible form of cheapness is net cash relative to market value, and it is only credible when earnings are not accrual-inflated; cash on the balance sheet cannot be manufactured by accounting choices.
evaluated.reasoning: Net-cash-to-price is a valuation anchor that HML (a book-based factor) spans poorly, so a spread built on it can retain raw return without inheriting the large value-factor loading that produced the archive's negative alphas. Requiring clean accruals alongside net cash separates genuinely cash-rich cheap firms from those whose apparent balance-sheet strength is receivables and inventory.

evaluated.name: EVYieldSloanAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Enterprise-value cheapness is credible only when operating profit is not generated by working-capital accruals net of depreciation; EV anchoring removes the leverage tilt that makes book-based value spreads collinear with HML.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-0's EV/EBITDA composite remains the best joint result in the archive (FMB 3.59, alpha ≈ 0, Sharpe 0.29) but used a fragile multi-item working-capital delta, while gen-3 showed the working-capital stock is the wrong quality variable. This version keeps the EV anchor and the accrual *change* but measures it with the compact wcap−dp Sloan definition, isolating whether measurement noise in the accrual leg was suppressing the EV composite's alpha.

evaluated.name: NetCashCleanValueTriple
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is trustworthy when it is simultaneously visible in book value, backed by net cash on the balance sheet, and not manufactured by accruals; the cash channel screens out the levered value traps that dominate book-only value screens.
evaluated.reasoning: The net-cash anchor was the only channel producing positive FF5 alpha, and the book-value-plus-clean-accruals composite was among the strongest FMB slopes, so combining all three ranks tests directly whether the two forms of evidence can be obtained together rather than traded off. Ranking each channel also removes the skewness that made the raw net-cash ratio cross-sectionally weak.

evaluated.name: NetCashAccrualStability
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes cheap balance-sheet-strong firms safe is not the level of accruals but the predictability of their accrual process; erratic accruals signal earnings management and estimation error that will eventually reverse into write-downs.
evaluated.reasoning: Accrual volatility is an untested quality dimension in this archive and is close to orthogonal to the accrual level, so it can add information rather than restate the Sloan measure. Pairing it with the net-cash anchor keeps the spread out of deep-value territory, where every prior long leg was penalized by its HML and CMA loadings.

evaluated.name: SalesToEVRevenueQuality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Revenue-based cheapness measured against total enterprise value, combined with improving cash conversion of revenue, identifies firms whose sales are real and whose capital structure does not disguise expensiveness.
evaluated.reasoning: The sales-yield plus revenue-quality channel produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.332) but a negative alpha because price-only deflation loads the long leg with highly levered value names; deflating by EV penalizes debt and tilts the long leg toward the net-cash firms that generated positive alpha. This isolates the deflator choice while holding the revenue-quality mechanism fixed.

evaluated.name: PayoutCoverageRankGap
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm whose dividend yield rank far exceeds its accrual-purged cash-earnings yield rank is distributing cash it does not generate, and that unsustainable payout precedes dividend cuts and negative returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The level version of this payout-coverage idea had the strongest correctly-signed FMB slope in the archive (−2.44) but a wrong-signed decile alpha, which is what happens when a price-deflated level's extreme tail is populated by distressed rebound names rather than by the economically intended cases. Differencing two rank-transformed yields bounds the signal, makes the sorted deciles reflect the same monotone relation the FMB slope detects, and keeps the construction nearly value-factor neutral since both legs are price-deflated yields.

evaluated.name: DebtFinancedAccrualTrap
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: The prototypical value trap is cheap because of leverage, not because of mispricing, and its reported profits are accrual-driven; net debt per dollar of market value combined with high accruals identifies firms whose equity is an option on deteriorating accounting.
evaluated.reasoning: This makes the financing channel the explicit driver rather than a by-product, and it is the economic mirror of the net-cash signal that produced the archive's only positive alpha, so it should inherit a correctly signed (negative) alpha while sharpening the short side. Because both legs are elevated for levered accrual-heavy firms, the sort concentrates on a specific, identifiable trap population instead of the broad value universe.

evaluated.name: NetCashValueConservativeDep
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(dp, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness supported by net cash and by conservative depreciation policy identifies firms whose low price reflects understated accounting earnings rather than deteriorating economics.
evaluated.reasoning: This keeps the winning net-cash-plus-book-value frame but swaps the working-capital accrual screen for the long-lived-asset accrual channel, which had the archive's strongest FMB slope (3.98) and the highest coverage (0.137) because it needs no lagged data. If alpha stays near +0.03 while FMB rises above 3, the depreciation channel dominates the Sloan channel and should anchor the final refinement.

evaluated.name: GrossCashValueCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The FF5-orthogonal component of the winning signal comes from holding hard, unmanipulable cash relative to price, not from low leverage per se.
evaluated.reasoning: Net cash mixes a cash-asset effect with a negative-leverage effect, and FF5 partially prices leverage through HML and CMA, so replacing net cash with gross cash-to-price cleanly attributes the +0.029 alpha to one of the two. This is a deliberate single-design-choice isolation whose outcome determines whether later generations should push the cash-asset story or the low-leverage story.

evaluated.name: NetCashSalesEVRevenueQuality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Combining the balance-sheet cash channel with revenue-based enterprise cheapness and clean accruals should retain the strongest cross-sectional signal in the archive while inheriting the alpha-generating cash dimension.
evaluated.reasoning: Sales-to-EV plus revenue quality produced the best FMB t-stat (3.81) and Sharpe (0.36) but a mildly negative alpha, whereas net cash produced reliable positive alpha with weak cross-sectional power; the two channels have complementary failure modes. If both statistics strengthen relative to NetCashCleanValueTriple, the revenue multiple is a better cheapness anchor than book equity within the cash-backed frame.

evaluated.name: NetCashValuePercentAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), ABS(ib)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically relevant question is what share of *earnings* is accrual-based, not what share of assets; deflating accruals by the magnitude of income sharpens the value-trap screen.
evaluated.reasoning: Percent accruals were only ever tested inside the failed indicator-gating structure, where degenerate portfolios masked their information content, so this re-tests the measure inside the frame that demonstrably works. Winsorizing controls the small-earnings denominators that make percent accruals explosive, addressing the tail problem that flipped earlier level-based signals' decile spreads.

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryCheapCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm that is cheap relative to its own five-year valuation history, while its earnings remain cash-backed, has been de-rated without accounting deterioration — a mispricing rather than a fundamental repricing.
evaluated.reasoning: Time-series cheapness is measured within firm, so it carries little cross-sectional book-to-market tilt and should not be absorbed by HML the way every level-based value composite in the archive was. Pairing it with the accrual screen keeps the economic interaction intact: a de-rating is an opportunity only if the accounting behind current earnings has not degraded.

evaluated.name: LeveredPayoutAccrualTrap
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))))

evaluated.hypothesis: Conservative depreciation understates the earnings and book value of cash-rich, low-debt cheap firms, making their apparent cheapness a measurement artifact that reverses as cash flows are recognized.

evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The value trap is a cheap firm distributing dividends it does not earn in cash while carrying net debt and accrual-inflated profits; payout coverage is the monotone core of the mechanism and leverage and accruals intensify it.

evaluated.name: CheapWithCashCoverage
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), lct))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is defensible when accrual-purged cash earnings can service near-term obligations; a cheap firm whose current liabilities dwarf its cash earnings faces forced asset sales and equity dilution regardless of book value.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a new economic channel — near-term solvency coverage rather than balance-sheet composition — and it interacts the two themes multiplicatively in the denominator by measuring cash earnings against the current liabilities that generated much of the accrual. Current liabilities are almost never zero, so the ratio is far better behaved than the debt-to-price measures whose skewness has been suppressing FMB slopes.

evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings that generate a tax liability have been validated by an outside authority, so cheap, cash-rich firms carrying taxes payable are reporting real income, whereas accrual-inflated earnings typically create book-tax differences and no tax accrual.
evaluated.reasoning: The tax channel is the one accrual dimension in the resource menu never yet tested, and it is economically distinct from working-capital accruals because it reflects external verification rather than management estimates. evaluated.name: CashDebtSplitDualQuality

evaluated.name: CashDebtSplitTaxQuality

evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings that generate a tax liability are externally verified, so tax-confirmed profits are the cheapest available proof that a low-priced firm's income is real rather than accrued.

evaluated.hypothesis: If accounting quality is the binding constraint on whether cheapness pays, it deserves more than an equal share of the composite; doubling its weight should sharpen the separation between genuine value and value traps.

evaluated.name: CashBackedCleanValueConjunction

evaluated.hypothesis: Balance-sheet strength and cheap-clean accounting are complements: a firm must clear both hurdles, so the weaker of the two composite ranks should determine expected returns rather than their average.
evaluated.reasoning: Averaging lets an extreme cash position offset accrual-inflated earnings, which is precisely the substitution the value-trap story says should not be allowed, and the MIN operator enforces the conjunction while leaving both economic channels unchanged. evaluated.name: CashPoorLeveredPayoutTrap

evaluated.name: SplitCashFlowStatementAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RATIO(dp, at))))

The trade-off is coverage, since oancf begins later, so the comparison against the wcap-based version quantifies whether measurement completeness is worth the sample loss.

evaluated.name: TaxUnconfirmedLeveredTrap
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(RATIO(txp, at))), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A cash-poor, levered firm paying dividends it does not earn, whose accrual-driven profits generate no tax liability, is reporting income that exists only on paper and should underperform reliably.
evaluated.reasoning: The trap composite already produces the archive's largest abnormal return (alpha −0.067, t = −4.41) but its FMB stalls near −1.8 because the effect concentrates in the extreme tail; the absence of a tax liability is a broadly distributed, monotone indicator of unverified earnings that should extend the signal into the middle of the cross-section. Adding it tests whether the short-side mechanism can be made cross-sectionally monotone without sacrificing portfolio alpha.

evaluated.name: IndNeutralSplitCleanValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))))

evaluated.name: SplitHardBookValue

evaluated.hypothesis: Rather than screening cheapness with a separate accrual score, the accrual correction belongs inside the value measure itself: book equity stripped of non-cash working capital is the portion of book value that cannot be written down.

Because gen-7 showed that adding weight to a standalone accrual channel hurt alpha, the alternative of building quality into the value measure is the natural remaining design question.

evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is trustworthy when it appears both in operating profit per dollar of enterprise value and in book equity stripped of soft non-cash working capital, held by a cash-rich, low-debt firm.
evaluated.reasoning: These are the archive's two best-performing value channels — EBITDA/EV owns the strongest cross-sectional slope and Sharpe, hard book-to-market the strongest alpha t-statistic — and they contaminate differently, since one bypasses the balance sheet entirely while the other cleans it. Combining exactly four equally weighted channels respects the finding that quarter-weights maximize alpha and that further breadth dilutes it.

evaluated.name: SplitEbitdaEVCashFlowAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dpc), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The sharpest measure of accrual reliance is net income minus operating cash flow with depreciation added back, since it captures every non-depreciation accrual directly from the cash-flow statement without balance-sheet differencing error.
evaluated.reasoning: The cash-flow-statement accrual definition delivered the archive's largest alpha (0.060) but was bundled with book value and depreciation, leaving its slope weak (2.01); pairing it instead with the highest-slope value anchor should supply the cross-sectional monotonicity it lacked. Adding depreciation back isolates exactly the discretionary accruals the value-trap story concerns, rather than mixing them with capital-intensity effects.

evaluated.name: SplitHardBookCashFlowAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), lct)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dpc), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheap firms whose book value consists of hard assets and whose earnings are confirmed by operating cash flow are the purest expression of quality-supported value; the balance sheet and the cash-flow statement must agree.
evaluated.reasoning: This pairs the two ingredients with the highest alpha t-statistics in the archive (4.43 and 3.59) and they are conceptually complementary: one removes soft assets from the stock measure of value, the other removes soft earnings from the flow measure of profit. If alpha exceeds 0.055 with t above 4, the interaction is confirmed on both financial statements simultaneously rather than through a single accrual proxy.

evaluated.name: SplitEbitdaEVHardBookSloan

evaluated.hypothesis: An explicit flow-based accrual screen still adds information beyond an accrual-corrected book value, because stripping soft assets from the balance sheet says nothing about how fast those assets are currently being built.

evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Value and quality can be fused into a single channel — the price paid per dollar of accrual-purged cash earnings — and given half the total weight alongside the cash and debt channels, without needing separate value and quality ranks.

It is the most parsimonious version of the whole research idea, and if it matches the four-channel composites, the mechanism reduces to cash-backed cash earnings.

evaluated.name: SplitNoLagBroadCoverage

This tests whether roughly a quarter more firm-months can be signalled without losing the abnormal return, which matters for whether the result is an implementable strategy or a narrow-sample artifact.

considered.name: CashBackedBookToMarket
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Book-to-market predicts returns only when reported earnings are backed by operating cash flow; cheap firms whose income is accrual-driven are value traps whose book value will be written down.
considered.reasoning: The first channel ranks cheapness, the second ranks accounting quality as the negative of total accruals (ib - oancf) scaled by assets, so the composite is high only for firms that are simultaneously cheap and cash-generating. This isolates "high-quality value" from mechanically cheap distressed accrual firms, which should raise both the cross-sectional slope and the FF5 spread alpha versus plain B/M.

considered.name: ValueGatedByCashSurplus
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Value exposure should be taken only in the state where accruals are negative (cash flow exceeds reported income); in the positive-accrual state cheapness carries no reliable premium.
considered.reasoning: The indicator turns the valuation rank on only when total accruals are negative, so the signal is a state-dependent value bet rather than a linear blend of two themes. If the value premium is concentrated in cash-surplus firms, the conditional version should show a stronger long-short FF5 alpha per unit of turnover than unconditional B/M.

considered.name: AccrualYieldOnPrice
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: Deflating accruals by market value rather than assets measures how much of the price-implied earnings claim is non-cash; a large accrual claim per dollar of market equity is the defining feature of a value trap.
considered.reasoning: Because the deflator is price, this variable is jointly high for cheap firms and for accrual-heavy firms, so it mechanically pinpoints the intersection the economic story targets instead of either theme alone. Firms with high accrual-to-price should underperform as accruals reverse and the apparent cheapness disappears.

considered.name: EVYieldCleanWorkingCapital
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Enterprise-level cheapness (EBITDA/EV) is trustworthy only when operating profitability is not being manufactured by working-capital build-ups in receivables and inventory.
considered.reasoning: EBITDA/EV neutralizes leverage and cash holdings so cheapness is measured on operating assets, while the change in non-cash working capital captures the specific accrual channel (receivables/inventory inflation) that contaminates EBITDA. Combining them should separate genuinely cheap operating businesses from those whose EBITDA is a working-capital illusion.

considered.name: CashMinusEarningsYieldGap
considered.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
considered.hypothesis: The market prices visible earnings yield but underweights cash-flow yield; firms that look expensive on earnings but cheap on cash flow are mispriced upward-revision candidates, and the reverse for accrual-inflated earnings.
considered.reasoning: The signal is the valuation wedge created purely by accruals, since the two ratios share the same price deflator and differ only by (ib - oancf). It directly tests whether investors anchor on accrual-laden earnings multiples and therefore misprice cash-based cheapness, which is the accrual-anomaly mechanism expressed in valuation space.

considered.name: EarningsYieldAccrualStability
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A high earnings yield is a reliable value signal only if the firm's accrual behavior is stable; volatile accruals indicate low-quality, easily reversed earnings and hence an unreliable multiple.
considered.reasoning: Rather than penalizing the level of accruals, this uses five-year accrual volatility as a measure of accounting reliability, a distinct quality dimension that captures earnings-management intensity and estimation error. Cheap firms with quiet, predictable accruals should deliver the value premium, while cheap firms with erratic accruals should not, sharpening both the Fama-MacBeth slope and the FF5 alpha.

considered.name: ValueCleanSloanAccruals
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Book-to-market earns a premium only when reported profits are not produced by working-capital build-up net of depreciation; accrual-heavy cheap firms are value traps.
considered.reasoning: The accrual leg is the balance-sheet Sloan measure (change in working capital minus depreciation) scaled by assets, built from theme-exclusive items `wcap` and `dp` that are reported far more broadly than cash-flow-statement components, which should lift coverage well above the 0.11 of the accepted gen-0 signal. Ranking both legs makes the long book cheap-and-clean and the short book expensive-and-accrual-laden, the exact intersection the economic story requires.
